newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EURO-defence group to give Turkey more access.
newsitem.headline: EURO-defence group to give Turkey more access.

text.p: The Western European Union (WEU), the European Union's emerging defence body, agreed on Tuesday a deal giving non-members Turkey and Norway a full role in any operations launched with NATO equipment, diplomats said.

The deal was hailed as a major step towards creating a greater European identity within the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation -- a key demand of France for a full return to the military side of the alliance it quit in 1966.
"We are absolutely delighted with this deal, it takes us one great step nearer establishing a European security and defence identity," said one western diplomat.
Turkey and Norway are currently members of NATO, but only associate members of the 10-nation WEU -- made up of members of the European Union except Ireland, Finland, Sweden, Austria and Denmark.

Under plans to give the WEU greater teeth, but stop a duplication of defence efforts the United States -- by far NATO's most important member -- has agreed to allow the WEU to use its equipment for European-only operations.

The plan risked falling apart when NATO member Turkey, already feeling shunned by EU governments, said it would veto any use of NATO equipment and infrastructure by the WEU unless it was involved in the planning and organising of future European operations.
